-- Difficulty: non-obvious
-- Import stratum: composition
--
-- The normal subgroup of a congruence equivalent (through φ) to the congruence of a normal subgroup N is N.
--
module Group-normal-of-equivalent-congruence where

open import AgdaDojang.Debug

open import Data.Product                            using ( proj₁ )
open import Level                                   using ( Level )
open import Classical.Structures.Group.Basic        using ( Group )
open import Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences  using ( module GroupCongruences )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Basic                using ( Con )
open import Setoid.Congruences.Lattice              using ( _≑_ ; ≑-refl )

module _ {α ρ ℓ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) where

  open GroupCongruences 𝒢  using ( NormalSubgroup ; normalOf ; congruenceOf ; _≈ⁿ_ ; ≈ⁿ-refl )

  normal-of-equivalent-congruence : {θ φ : Con (proj₁ 𝒢) ℓ} {𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ}
    → θ ≑ φ → φ ≑ congruenceOf 𝑵 → normalOf θ ≈ⁿ 𝑵
  normal-of-equivalent-congruence {θ} {φ} {𝑵} θ≑φ φ≑N = {!!}

6	author: "the agda-algebras development team"
7	---
8	
9	### Normal subgroups and congruences of a group
10	
11	This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].
12	
13	The normal subgroups of a group `𝒢` correspond to the congruences of the underlying
14	`Sig-Group`-algebra.  This module establishes that correspondence as an **order
15	isomorphism of posets**, between the congruence poset `(Con 𝑮 ℓ , ≑ , ⊑)` of
16	[Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][] and the poset `(NormalSubgroup ℓ , ≈ⁿ , ≤ⁿ)` of normal
17	subgroups under inclusion, which is built here.
18	
19	Both sides carry more structure than a poset: at the absorbing level `L` the
20	congruences form a complete lattice ([Setoid.Congruences.CompleteLattice][]).  The
21	corresponding **isomorphism of complete lattices** is
22	[Classical.Structures.Group.NormalSubgroupLattice][], which stands on the poset
23	isomorphism proved here.  The split is deliberate: the correspondence below holds at
24	*every* relation level, whereas a lattice needs the single absorbing level at which
25	the join — a *generated* congruence — stays put, so bundling them would have narrowed
26	the theorem to the level the lattice happens to need.
27	
28	The correspondence has two mutually inverse, order-preserving maps.
29	
30	+  **`N ↦ θ_N`** (`congruenceOf`{.AgdaFunction}).  A normal subgroup `N` maps to the
31	   relation `NormalRel`{.AgdaFunction}` N`, defined by `x θ_N y ⟺ x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N`.
32	   We prove that this is an equivalence containing the setoid equality (for which
33	   `N`{.AgdaBound} being an equality-respecting subgroup is enough) and
34	   compatible with the three operations of `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction}, which is where
35	   normality is consumed.
36	
37	+  **`θ ↦ N_θ`** (`normalOf`{.AgdaFunction}).  A congruence `θ`{.AgdaBound} maps to
38	   the `θ`-class of the identity; we define the latter as
39	   `IdentityClass`{.AgdaFunction} `θ`{.AgdaBound}, which represents the predicate
40	   `{ x ∣ x θ ε }`.  We prove it is a normal, equality-respecting subgroup.
41	
42	The two maps are monotone and mutually inverse — up to `≑`{.AgdaFunction} on
43	congruences and mutual inclusion on normal subgroups — so together they are an
44	`OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} of [Order.Iso][].
45	
46	This is the bridge that `Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormal` was written
47	without: it lets us apply the library's `IsSubdirectlyIrreducible`{.AgdaFunction} of
48	[Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][] — a statement about `Con 𝑨`{.AgdaFunction} — to a
49	group, whose subdirect irreducibility the group theorist states as "there is a
50	least nontrivial normal subgroup".  The final step of that identification,
51	`HasMonolithᵍ → HasMonolith`, is deliberately *not* taken here; see **What this module
52	does and does not transport** below.
53	
54	Four points about the formal statement deserve to be recorded up front, because in each
55	case the informal slogan "congruences are normal subgroups" conceals a choice that the
56	mechanized version has to make.
57	
58	+  **The correspondence is level-uniform, not level-collapsing**.  It relates
59	   `Con 𝑮 ℓ`{.AgdaFunction} to `NormalSubgroup ℓ`{.AgdaFunction} for each *fixed*
60	   relation level `ℓ`{.AgdaBound}, since `NormalRel`{.AgdaFunction} of a `Pred G ℓ` is
61	   a `BinaryRel G ℓ` and `IdentityClass`{.AgdaFunction} of a `Con 𝑮 ℓ` is a
62	   `Pred G ℓ`.  It says nothing about congruences at one level versus normal subgroups
63	   at another.  Three instances matter downstream: `ℓ = ρ`, where the congruence side
64	   is the `Con 𝑮 ρ` of `IsMonolith`{.AgdaRecord} and the subgroup side contains
65	   `trivialSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction}, itself a `Subgroup ρ`; `ℓ = α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀`, the
66	   absorbing level of the congruence lattice, which is where
67	   [Classical.Structures.Group.NormalSubgroupLattice][] instantiates it; and
68	   `ℓ = α ⊔ ℓ₀`, the predicate level `L` at which `GroupSublattice 𝒢 ℓ₀`{.AgdaModule}
69	   of [Classical.Structures.Group.SubgroupLattice][] holds its elements, for a
70	   consumer that wants to compose with the *subgroup* lattice.
71	
72	+  **Equality on each side is mutual containment, not propositional equality**.  On the
73	   congruence side this is `_≑_`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][], for
74	   the reasons given there (upgrading it would need propositional extensionality, which
75	   `--safe --cubical-compatible` does not provide); on the subgroup side we take the
76	   matching `_≈ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction}.  So `to∘from`{.AgdaField} and `from∘to`{.AgdaField}
77	   are *bi-implications of membership*, not equalities of predicates.
78	
79	+  **The round trip on subgroups uses the `respects`{.AgdaField} field**.  Recovering
80	   `N`{.AgdaBound} from `θ_N` produces `{ x ∣ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N }`, and identifying that with
81	   `N`{.AgdaBound} moves membership across `x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x`.  A normal *subuniverse* that
82	   does not respect the setoid equality therefore need not be recovered by the round
83	   trip, exactly as in the respecting-interval finding of [FLRP.Bridge][].  This is why
84	   `NormalSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} is built on `IsSubgroup`{.AgdaRecord} (which carries
85	   `respects`{.AgdaField}) rather than on bare `Subuniverses`{.AgdaFunction}.
86	
87	+  **Normality is consumed only by compatibility, and it is consumed exactly**.  For an
88	   arbitrary equality-respecting subgroup `N`{.AgdaBound}, `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction}
89	   is already an equivalence relation containing `_≈_`{.AgdaFunction}; this is
90	   `SubgroupRel`{.AgdaModule} below, and it holds with no normality hypothesis.  What
91	   needs normality is compatibility with `∙-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} and
92	   `⁻¹-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor}, so the separation is stated rather than folded
93	   into one monolithic lemma — and the converse `congruence→normal`{.AgdaFunction} is
94	   proved, so that "the correspondence is with the *normal* subgroups" is a theorem of
95	   the module and not a claim its prose makes on the development's behalf.
96	
97	**On the choice of relation**.  `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` is the *right*-coset relation of
98	`N`{.AgdaBound}, whereas `Coset._∼_`{.AgdaFunction} of
99	[Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][] — the relation [FLRP.Bridge][] uses — is the
100	*left*-coset relation `x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ N`.  For a general subgroup the two need not agree;
101	for a normal subgroup they do, which we prove (`rel→coset`{.AgdaFunction},
102	`coset→rel`{.AgdaFunction}) rather than assume, so that either presentation may be used
103	downstream.
104	
105	**What this module does and does not transport**.  The first notion carried whole
106	across the correspondence is simplicity: the final section below proves that the
107	group-theoretic `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] is
108	equivalent to the congruence-level `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of
109	[Setoid.Congruences.Simple][], constructively in both directions.  The retirement
110	program built on the correspondence also asks that `HasMonolithᵍ`{.AgdaFunction} of
111	`Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormal` be transported to
112	`HasMonolith`{.AgdaFunction}, that the `ᵍ` superscript be retired, and that `𝒢₂` of
113	`FLRP.Reductions` be restated.  Those steps remain open, with the simplicity
114	equivalence as their template; the `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction}/nontriviality equivalences
115	proved here (`nonzero→nontrivial`{.AgdaFunction} and friends) are precisely the
116	ingredient the monolith transport will need beyond the isomorphism itself.

169	
170	#### The ambient group
171	
172	Everything below is developed inside one parameterized module, so that the group, its
173	carrier, its curried operations, and the conjugation vocabulary are fixed once.
174	
175	```agda
176	module GroupCongruences {α ρ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) where
177	  private
178	    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
179	    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]
180	
181	  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]            using  ( _≈_ )
182	                                renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
183	  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
184	  open Group-Op 𝒢               using  ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; assoc-law
185	                                       ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
186	  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ  using  ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙
187	                                       ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
188	  open Conjugate 𝒢                   using  ( conj-syntax ; conj-ε ; IsNormal )
189	```
190	
191	#### Four facts of group arithmetic
192	
193	The correspondence rests on four small identities, each named so that no proof below
194	has to inline an equational chain about them.  The first two say that `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε`
195	is *equivalent* to `x ≈ y` — this is what makes the relation `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` collapse to
196	the setoid equality exactly when `N` is trivial.  The third is right-cancellation in the
197	form the round trip needs, and the fourth is the unit law that identifies `x ∙ ε ⁻¹`
198	with `x`.
199	
200	```agda
201	  -- x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε implies x ≈ y (multiply on the right by y).
202	  ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ : ∀ {x y} → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε → x ≈ y
203	  ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ {x} {y} h = begin
204	    x               ≈˘⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
205	    x ∙ ε           ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (invˡ-law y) ⟩
206	    x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ y)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) y ⟩
207	    x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y    ≈⟨ ∙-cong h ≈refl ⟩
208	    ε ∙ y           ≈⟨ idˡ-law y ⟩
209	    y               ∎
210	
211	  -- ... and conversely, equal elements have trivial right quotient.
212	  ≈→∙⁻¹≈ε : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε
213	  ≈→∙⁻¹≈ε {x} {y} x≈y = ≈trans (∙-cong x≈y ≈refl) (invʳ-law y)
214	
215	  -- Right cancellation: the right quotient by y, multiplied back by y, is the identity.
216	  ∙⁻¹∙ : ∀ x y → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y ≈ x
217	  ∙⁻¹∙ x y = begin
218	    x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y    ≈⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) y ⟩
219	    x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ y)  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (invˡ-law y) ⟩
220	    x ∙ ε           ≈⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
221	    x               ∎
222	
223	  -- The right quotient by the identity is the identity map.
224	  ∙ε⁻¹ : ∀ x → x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x
225	  ∙ε⁻¹ x = ≈trans (∙-cong ≈refl ε⁻¹≈ε) (idʳ-law x)
226	```
227	
228	#### Normal subgroups as an ordered object
229	
230	A **normal subgroup** of `𝒢`{.AgdaBound} at predicate level `ℓ`{.AgdaBound} is a
231	predicate on the carrier together with a proof that it is an equality-respecting
232	subgroup and a proof that it is closed under conjugation.  This is
233	`Subgroup`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] with
234	`IsNormal`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation][] adjoined; it is
235	introduced here rather than there because normality is the *only* extra datum the
236	correspondence needs, and no earlier module had cause to bundle it.
237	
238	Normal subgroups are ordered by inclusion of the underlying predicates, with equality
239	mutual inclusion — the same shape as `_⊑_`{.AgdaFunction} and `_≑_`{.AgdaFunction} on
240	congruences, so that the isomorphism below can be stated without any bridging
241	construction on either side.
242	
243	```agda
244	  -- A normal subgroup: an equality-respecting subgroup closed under conjugation.
245	  NormalSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
246	  NormalSubgroup ℓ = Σ[ N ∈ Pred G ℓ ] (IsSubgroup 𝒢 N × IsNormal N)
247	
248	  -- The underlying predicate of a normal subgroup ...
249	  set : NormalSubgroup ℓ → Pred G ℓ
250	  set (N , _ , _) = N
251	
252	  -- ... and its two proof components.
253	  set-isSubgroup : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → IsSubgroup 𝒢 (set 𝑵)
254	  set-isSubgroup (_ , isSubgroup , _) = isSubgroup
255	
256	  set-normal : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → IsNormal (set 𝑵)
257	  set-normal (_ , _ , isNormal) = isNormal
258	
259	  infix 4 _≤ⁿ_ _≈ⁿ_
260	
261	  -- The inclusion order on normal subgroups ...
262	  _≤ⁿ_ : NormalSubgroup ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
263	  𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 = set 𝑴 ⊆ set 𝑵
264	
265	  -- ... and the equivalence of mutual inclusion it is antisymmetric over.
266	  _≈ⁿ_ : NormalSubgroup ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
267	  𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 = 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 × 𝑵 ≤ⁿ 𝑴
268	```
269	
270	Calling the correspondence an *order* isomorphism presupposes that both sides really
271	are ordered, so the partial-order laws are proved rather than assumed.  They are the
272	laws of `_⊆_`{.AgdaFunction} on predicates, and antisymmetry holds by construction:
273	`_≈ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction} *is* mutual inclusion.  This mirrors
274	`⊆-isPartialOrder`{.AgdaFunction} and `Con-Poset`{.AgdaFunction} on the congruence
275	side, down to the same implicit-argument discipline — `_≤ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction} is a
276	defined relation, not an injective type former, so Agda cannot recover the endpoint
277	arguments of the helper lemmas from the expected field types and they are forwarded by
278	hand.
279	
280	```agda
281	  ≤ⁿ-refl : {𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑵 ≤ⁿ 𝑵
282	  ≤ⁿ-refl p = p
283	
284	  ≤ⁿ-trans : {𝑳 𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑳 ≤ⁿ 𝑴 → 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑳 ≤ⁿ 𝑵
285	  ≤ⁿ-trans 𝑳≤𝑴 𝑴≤𝑵 p = 𝑴≤𝑵 (𝑳≤𝑴 p)
286	
287	  ≈ⁿ-refl : {𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑵 ≈ⁿ 𝑵
288	  ≈ⁿ-refl = (λ p → p) , (λ p → p)
289	
290	  ≈ⁿ-sym : {𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑵 ≈ⁿ 𝑴
291	  ≈ⁿ-sym = swap
292	
293	  ≈ⁿ-trans : {𝑳 𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑳 ≈ⁿ 𝑴 → 𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑳 ≈ⁿ 𝑵
294	  ≈ⁿ-trans (𝑳≤𝑴 , 𝑴≤𝑳) (𝑴≤𝑵 , 𝑵≤𝑴) = (λ p → 𝑴≤𝑵 (𝑳≤𝑴 p)) , (λ p → 𝑴≤𝑳 (𝑵≤𝑴 p))
295	
296	  ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ})
297	  ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence {ℓ} = record
298	    { refl   = λ {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-refl {ℓ} {𝑵}
299	    ; sym    = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-sym {ℓ} {𝑴} {𝑵}
300	    ; trans  = λ {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-trans {ℓ} {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵}
301	    }
302	
303	  ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder : IsPartialOrder (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ}) _≤ⁿ_
304	  ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder {ℓ} = record
305	    { isPreorder = record  { isEquivalence  = ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence {ℓ}
306	                           ; reflexive      = proj₁
307	                           ; trans          = λ {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≤ⁿ-trans {ℓ} {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵}
308	                           }
309	    ; antisym = _,_
310	    }
311	
312	  -- The poset of normal subgroups, the counterpart of `Con-Poset` of
313	  -- [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][].
314	  NormalSubgroup-Poset : (ℓ : Level) → Poset (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
315	  NormalSubgroup-Poset ℓ = record  { Carrier         = NormalSubgroup ℓ
316	                                   ; _≈_             = _≈ⁿ_
317	                                   ; _≤_             = _≤ⁿ_
318	                                   ; isPartialOrder  = ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder
319	                                   }
320	```
321	
322	#### The relation attached to a subgroup
323	
324	`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is the relation "`x` and `y` differ by an element of
325	`N`", written with the *right* quotient `x ∙ y ⁻¹`.  It is defined for an arbitrary
326	predicate, so that the hypotheses each of its properties needs can be stated exactly.
327	
328	```agda
329	  -- x and y are related when their right quotient lies in N.
330	  NormalRel : Pred G ℓ → BinaryRel G ℓ
331	  NormalRel N x y = x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N
332	```
333	
334	For an equality-respecting subgroup `N`{.AgdaBound} — with no normality hypothesis —
335	`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is an equivalence relation that contains the setoid
336	equality.  Each clause is one closure property of `N`{.AgdaBound} transported along one
337	line of group arithmetic, exactly as in `Coset`{.AgdaModule} of
338	[Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][] for the left-handed relation.
339	
340	```agda
341	  module SubgroupRel {ℓ : Level} (N : Pred G ℓ) (N-sg : IsSubgroup 𝒢 N) where
342	
343	    open IsSubgroup N-sg  using ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed ; ⁻¹-closed )
344	
345	    infix 4 _∼_
346	
347	    _∼_ : BinaryRel G ℓ
348	    _∼_ = NormalRel N
349	
350	    -- Reflexivity is ε ∈ N transported along x ∙ x ⁻¹ ≈ ε.
351	    ∼-refl : ∀ {x} → x ∼ x
352	    ∼-refl {x} = respects (≈sym (invʳ-law x)) ε-closed
353	
354	    -- Symmetry is closure under inverses, since (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ∙ x ⁻¹.
355	    ∼-sym : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → y ∼ x
356	    ∼-sym {x} {y} x∼y = respects inv-eq (⁻¹-closed x∼y)
357	      where
358	      inv-eq : (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ∙ x ⁻¹
359	      inv-eq = begin
360	        (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ x (y ⁻¹) ⟩
361	        (y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ x ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive y) ≈refl ⟩
362	        y ∙ x ⁻¹          ∎
363	
364	    -- Transitivity is closure under products, since (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ z ⁻¹.
365	    ∼-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x ∼ y → y ∼ z → x ∼ z
366	    ∼-trans {x} {y} {z} x∼y y∼z = respects prod-eq (∙-closed x∼y y∼z)
367	      where
368	      prod-eq : (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ z ⁻¹
369	      prod-eq = begin
370	        (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹)  ≈⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ⟩
371	        x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ y (z ⁻¹)) ⟩
372	        x ∙ z ⁻¹                 ∎
373	
374	    ∼-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _∼_
375	    ∼-isEquivalence = record { refl = ∼-refl ; sym = ∼-sym ; trans = ∼-trans }
376	
377	    -- The setoid equality refines the relation (this is the `reflexive` field a
378	    -- congruence must supply, and it is what makes the relation contain the diagonal).
379	    ≈⇒∼ : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∼ y
380	    ≈⇒∼ x≈y = respects (≈sym (≈→∙⁻¹≈ε x≈y)) ε-closed
381	
382	    -- Consequently the relation may be transported along ≈ in either argument.
383	    ∼-resp : ∀ {x x' y y'} → x ≈ x' → y ≈ y' → x ∼ y → x' ∼ y'
384	    ∼-resp x≈x' y≈y' p = ∼-trans (∼-trans (≈⇒∼ (≈sym x≈x')) p) (≈⇒∼ y≈y')
385	```

387	#### From a normal subgroup to a congruence
388	
389	Adding normality makes the relation compatible with the three operations of
390	`Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction}, hence a congruence.
391	
392	Compatibility with `∙-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} is the substantive clause and the
393	only one that uses normality in an essential way: from `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` and
394	`u ∙ v ⁻¹ ∈ N` we must produce `(x ∙ u) ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹ ∈ N`, and the two given elements do
395	not multiply to it — one of them must first be *moved past* `x`{.AgdaBound}, which is
396	precisely conjugation.  Compatibility with `⁻¹-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} is one
397	conjugation as well; with `ε-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} it is reflexivity.
398	
399	```agda
400	  module NormalCon {ℓ : Level} (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) where
401	
402	    private
403	      N : Pred G ℓ
404	      N = set 𝑵
405	
406	    open IsSubgroup (set-isSubgroup 𝑵)  using ( respects ; ∙-closed )
407	    open SubgroupRel N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) public
408	
409	    normal : IsNormal N
410	    normal = set-normal 𝑵
411	
412	    -- Compatibility with the curried multiplication.  The element x ∙ y ⁻¹ is on the
413	    -- wrong side of x ∙ u, so u ∙ v ⁻¹ is first conjugated by x — the one step that
414	    -- normality supplies and that fails for a non-normal subgroup.
415	    ∼-∙ : ∀ {x y u v} → x ∼ y → u ∼ v → (x ∙ u) ∼ (y ∙ v)
416	    ∼-∙ {x} {y} {u} {v} p q = respects step (∙-closed (normal x q) p)
417	      where
418	      step : x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ u ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹
419	      step = begin
420	        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹)    ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹)) (x ⁻¹) (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⟩
421	        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ x (y ⁻¹)) ⟩
422	        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ y ⁻¹                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law x u (v ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
423	        x ∙ u ∙ v ⁻¹ ∙ y ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ∙ u) (v ⁻¹) (y ⁻¹) ⟩
424	        x ∙ u ∙ (v ⁻¹ ∙ y ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ y v) ⟩
425	        x ∙ u ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹                    ∎
426	
427	    -- Compatibility with the curried inverse: conjugating x ∙ y ⁻¹ by x ⁻¹ produces
428	    -- y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹, which is the relation the other way round.
429	    ∼-⁻¹ : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → x ⁻¹ ∼ y ⁻¹
430	    ∼-⁻¹ {x} {y} p = ∼-sym (respects step (normal (x ⁻¹) p))
431	      where
432	      step : x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹
433	      step = ∙-cong (\\-leftDividesʳ x (y ⁻¹)) ≈refl
434	
435	    -- Compatibility with every operation symbol.  Each clause is the corresponding
436	    -- curried fact, transported across the tuple-vs-curried interpretation bridges of
437	    -- [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups].
438	    ∼-compatible : 𝑮 ∣≈ _∼_
439	    ∼-compatible ∙-Op   {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 u))
440	                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 v))
441	                                            (∼-∙ (p 0F) (p 1F))
442	    ∼-compatible ε-Op   {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 u))
443	                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 v))
444	                                            ∼-refl
445	    ∼-compatible ⁻¹-Op  {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 u))
446	                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 v))
447	                                            (∼-⁻¹ (p 0F))
448	
449	    -- The relation of a normal subgroup is a congruence of the group algebra.
450	    ∼-isCongruence : IsCongruence 𝑮 _∼_
451	    ∼-isCongruence = mkcon ≈⇒∼ ∼-isEquivalence ∼-compatible
452	```

454	For a normal subgroup the right-handed relation used here agrees with the left-handed
455	coset relation `Coset._∼_`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][],

457	`∼-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} followed by an involutivity rewrite, so nothing about the
458	development depends on which of the two presentations a consumer prefers.

460	```agda
461	    -- The right-coset relation of a normal subgroup is its left-coset relation ...
462	    rel→coset : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → Coset._∼_ 𝒢 N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) x y
463	    rel→coset {x} {y} p = respects (∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-involutive y)) (∼-⁻¹ p)
464	
465	    -- ... and conversely.
466	    coset→rel : ∀ {x y} → Coset._∼_ 𝒢 N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) x y → x ∼ y
467	    coset→rel {x} {y} p = ∼-resp  (⁻¹-involutive x) (⁻¹-involutive y)
468	                                  (∼-⁻¹ (respects (∙-cong ≈refl (≈sym (⁻¹-involutive y))) p))

479	#### From a congruence to a normal subgroup
480	
481	In the other direction the ingredients are the curried consequences of a congruence's
482	compatibility: it is preserved by multiplication, by inversion, and hence by
483	conjugation.  These are read off from `is-compatible`{.AgdaFunction} at the canonical
484	tuples, with no interpretation bridge needed — the curried accessors of
485	`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule} are *defined* by applying the interpreted symbol to exactly
486	those tuples.
487	
488	```agda
489	  module ConNormal {ℓ : Level} ((_θ_ , θcon) : Con 𝑮 ℓ) where
490	
491	    -- The equivalence laws of θ, read off the record.
492	    θ-refl : ∀ {x} → x θ x
493	    θ-refl = IsEquivalence.refl (is-equivalence θcon)
494	
495	    θ-sym : ∀ {x y} → x θ y → y θ x
496	    θ-sym = IsEquivalence.sym (is-equivalence θcon)
497	
498	    θ-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x θ y → y θ z → x θ z
499	    θ-trans = IsEquivalence.trans (is-equivalence θcon)
500	
501	    -- A congruence relates ≈-equal elements.
502	    θ-reflexive : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x θ y
503	    θ-reflexive = reflexive θcon
504	
505	    -- Compatibility with the curried multiplication ...
506	    θ-∙ : ∀ {x y u v} → x θ y → u θ v → (x ∙ u) θ (y ∙ v)
507	    θ-∙ {x} {y} {u} {v} p q = is-compatible θcon ∙-Op λ { 0F → p ; 1F → q }
508	
509	    -- ... and with the curried inverse.
510	    θ-⁻¹ : ∀ {x y} → x θ y → (x ⁻¹) θ (y ⁻¹)
511	    θ-⁻¹ p = is-compatible θcon ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → p)
512	
513	    -- Hence conjugation by any element preserves the congruence.
514	    θ-conj : ∀ g {x y} → x θ y → x ^ g θ y ^ g
515	    θ-conj g {x} {y} p = θ-∙ (θ-∙ (θ-refl {x = g}) p) (θ-refl {x = g ⁻¹})
516	```

518	The class of the identity is an equality-respecting subgroup, and it is normal.
519	Membership is `x θ ε`, so each subgroup law is one application of the corresponding
520	compatibility fact followed by a `≈`-step that renormalizes the right-hand side back to
521	`ε`{.AgdaFunction}: `ε ∙ ε ≈ ε`, `ε ⁻¹ ≈ ε`, and `conj g ε ≈ ε`.
522	
523	```agda
524	    -- The θ-class of the identity.
525	    IdentityClass : Pred G ℓ
526	    IdentityClass x = x θ ε
527	
528	    -- It respects the setoid equality, because a congruence contains it.
529	    IdentityClass-respects : IdentityClass Respects _≈_
530	    IdentityClass-respects x≈y p = θ-trans (θ-reflexive (≈sym x≈y)) p
531	
532	    IdentityClass-ε : ε ∈ IdentityClass
533	    IdentityClass-ε = θ-refl
534	
535	    IdentityClass-∙ : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ IdentityClass → y ∈ IdentityClass
536	      → x ∙ y ∈ IdentityClass
537	    IdentityClass-∙ p q = θ-trans (θ-∙ p q) (θ-reflexive (idˡ-law ε))
538	
539	    IdentityClass-⁻¹ : ∀ {x} → x ∈ IdentityClass → x ⁻¹ ∈ IdentityClass
540	    IdentityClass-⁻¹ p = θ-trans (θ-⁻¹ p) (θ-reflexive ε⁻¹≈ε)
541	
542	    -- The identity class is an equality-respecting subgroup ...
543	    IdentityClass-isSubgroup : IsSubgroup 𝒢 IdentityClass
544	    IdentityClass-isSubgroup = mkIsSubgroup 𝒢  IdentityClass-respects IdentityClass-∙
545	                                               IdentityClass-ε IdentityClass-⁻¹
546	
547	    -- ... and it is normal, since conjugation fixes the identity.
548	    IdentityClass-normal : IsNormal IdentityClass
549	    IdentityClass-normal g p = θ-trans (θ-conj g p) (θ-reflexive (conj-ε g))
550	```

552	The backward map of the correspondence packages the class with its two proofs.
553	
554	```agda
555	  -- θ ↦ N_θ : a congruence gives a normal subgroup of the group.
556	  normalOf : Con 𝑮 ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ
557	  normalOf θ =  ConNormal.IdentityClass θ
558	             ,  ConNormal.IdentityClass-isSubgroup θ
559	             ,  ConNormal.IdentityClass-normal θ

562	#### Normality is necessary, not merely sufficient
563	
564	`NormalCon`{.AgdaModule} shows normality *suffices* for `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} to
565	be a congruence.  The converse holds too, and is worth proving rather than asserting:
566	were it left as prose, the claim "the correspondence is with the *normal* subgroups"
567	would be doing work the formal development had not done, and nothing would rule out the
568	relation of some non-normal subgroup slipping into `Con 𝑮 ℓ`{.AgdaFunction}.
569	
570	The proof needs no new group arithmetic.  If `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is a
571	congruence, its identity class is normal by
572	`IdentityClass-normal`{.AgdaFunction} — and that class is
573	`{ x ∣ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N }`, which `respects`{.AgdaField} identifies with
574	`N`{.AgdaBound} itself.
575	
576	```agda
577	  -- If the relation of an equality-respecting subgroup is a congruence, the subgroup
578	  -- is normal.  With `NormalCon.∼-isCongruence` this makes normality *equivalent* to
579	  -- compatibility, so `NormalSubgroup ℓ` is exactly the source of the correspondence.
580	  congruence→normal : {ℓ : Level} (N : Pred G ℓ) → IsSubgroup 𝒢 N
581	    →  IsCongruence 𝑮 (NormalRel N) → IsNormal N
582	  congruence→normal N N-sg isCon g {x} x∈N =
583	    respects  (∙ε⁻¹ (x ^ g))
584	              (ConNormal.IdentityClass-normal (NormalRel N , isCon) g
585	                (respects (≈sym (∙ε⁻¹ x)) x∈N))
586	    where open IsSubgroup N-sg using ( respects )
587	```

589	#### Monotonicity
590	
591	Both maps act by (co)restriction of the underlying predicates and relations, so
592	monotonicity is immediate in each direction.
593	
594	```agda
595	  -- The congruence-to-subgroup map is monotone.
596	  normalOf-mono : (θ φ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → θ ⊑ φ → normalOf θ ≤ⁿ normalOf φ
597	  normalOf-mono _ _ θ⊑φ p = θ⊑φ p
598	
599	  -- The subgroup-to-congruence map is monotone.
600	  congruenceOf-mono : (𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 → congruenceOf 𝑴 ⊑ congruenceOf 𝑵
601	  congruenceOf-mono _ _ 𝑴≤𝑵 p = 𝑴≤𝑵 p
602	```
603	
604	`OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} asks only for monotonicity, not for the maps to be well defined
605	on equivalence classes, so that latter property — which "isomorphism of posets" is
606	usually taken to include — is recorded here rather than left implicit.  It costs
607	nothing: each equivalence *is* mutual containment, so applying the matching
608	monotonicity twice suffices.
609	
610	```agda
611	  -- Both maps respect the equivalences of the two sides.
612	  normalOf-cong : (θ φ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → θ ≑ φ → normalOf θ ≈ⁿ normalOf φ
613	  normalOf-cong  θ φ (θ⊑φ , φ⊑θ) =
614	    normalOf-mono θ φ θ⊑φ , normalOf-mono φ θ φ⊑θ
615	
616	  congruenceOf-cong : (𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
617	    →  𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → congruenceOf 𝑴 ≑ congruenceOf 𝑵
618	  congruenceOf-cong 𝑴 𝑵 (𝑴≤𝑵 , 𝑵≤𝑴) =
619	    congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵 𝑴≤𝑵 , congruenceOf-mono 𝑵 𝑴 𝑵≤𝑴
620	```

622	#### Mutual inverseness
623	
624	On congruences, `θ_{N_θ} ≑ θ`: the relation `θ_{N_θ}` holds at `(x , y)` when
625	`(x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε`, and multiplying on the right by `y`{.AgdaBound} converts that to
626	`x θ y` through `∙⁻¹∙`{.AgdaFunction} and the unit law — while multiplying `x θ y` on
627	the right by `y ⁻¹` converts it back through `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.
628	
629	```agda
630	  -- Round trip on congruences: θ_{N_θ} ≑ θ.
631	  congruenceOf∘normalOf : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → congruenceOf (normalOf θ) ≑ θ
632	  congruenceOf∘normalOf θ = fwd , bwd
633	    where
634	    open ConNormal θ
635	
636	    -- From (x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε derive x θ y.
637	    fwd : congruenceOf (normalOf θ) ⊑ θ
638	    fwd {x} {y} p = θ-trans  (θ-reflexive (≈sym (∙⁻¹∙ x y)))
639	                             (θ-trans (θ-∙ p θ-refl) (θ-reflexive (idˡ-law y)))
640	
641	    -- From x θ y derive (x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε.
642	    bwd : θ ⊑ congruenceOf (normalOf θ)
643	    bwd {x} {y} p = θ-trans (θ-∙ p (θ-refl {y ⁻¹})) (θ-reflexive (invʳ-law y))
644	```

646	On normal subgroups, `N_{θ_N} ≈ⁿ N`: an element `x`{.AgdaBound} lies in `N_{θ_N}` when
647	`x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N`, and `x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x`, so the `respects`{.AgdaField} proof carried by the
648	subgroup identifies the two.  **This is the step that consumes the
649	`respects`{.AgdaField} field**, and the sole place the correspondence would break for a
650	normal subuniverse not closed under the setoid equality.
651	
652	```agda
653	  -- Round trip on normal subgroups: N_{θ_N} ≈ⁿ N (needs the respecting field).
654	  normalOf∘congruenceOf : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵) ≈ⁿ 𝑵
655	  normalOf∘congruenceOf 𝑵 = fwd , bwd
656	    where
657	    open IsSubgroup (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) using ( respects )
658	
659	    -- x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N and x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x give x ∈ N.
660	    fwd : normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵) ≤ⁿ 𝑵
661	    fwd {x} p = respects (∙ε⁻¹ x) p
662	
663	    -- x ∈ N and x ≈ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ give x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N.
664	    bwd : 𝑵 ≤ⁿ normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵)
665	    bwd {x} p = respects (≈sym (∙ε⁻¹ x)) p
666	```

668	#### The order isomorphism
669	
670	Assembling the four facts — two maps, both monotone, mutually inverse — gives the
671	correspondence as an `OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} between the congruence containment order of
672	the group algebra and the inclusion order on normal subgroups.  (The endpoint implicits
673	of the monotone maps are bound and forwarded explicitly: `Con`{.AgdaFunction} and
674	`NormalSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} are defined functions, not injective type formers, so
675	Agda cannot recover them from the field types.)

677	```agda

679	  NormalCongruenceIso : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
680	  NormalCongruenceIso ℓ =
681	    OrderIso (_≑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ}) (_⊑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ}) (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ}) (_≤ⁿ_ {ℓ})
682	
683	  normal-congruence-iso : (ℓ : Level) → NormalCongruenceIso ℓ
684	  normal-congruence-iso ℓ = record
685	    { to         = normalOf
686	    ; from       = congruenceOf
687	    ; to-mono    = λ {θ} {φ} → normalOf-mono θ φ
688	    ; from-mono  = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵
689	    ; to∘from    = normalOf∘congruenceOf
690	    ; from∘to    = congruenceOf∘normalOf
691	    }
692	```

705	    ; from       = normalOf
706	    ; to-mono    = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵
707	    ; from-mono  = λ {θ} {φ} → normalOf-mono θ φ
708	    ; to∘from    = congruenceOf∘normalOf
709	    ; from∘to    = normalOf∘congruenceOf

713	#### Nonzero congruences and nontrivial normal subgroups
714	
715	The order isomorphism alone does not say that the two sides agree on which elements are
716	*above the bottom*; that has to be proved, and it is what the monolith transport will
717	consume.  The bottom of the subgroup side is `trivialSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} of
718	[Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] — the `≈`-class of the identity, which over a
719	setoid carrier is the right notion of the one-element subgroup — and the bottom of the
720	congruence side is the diagonal, whose "at the bottom" predicate is
721	`BelowDiagonal`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][].
722	
723	```agda
724	  -- N is contained in the trivial subgroup { x ∣ x ≈ ε }.
725	  BelowTrivial : Pred G ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
726	  BelowTrivial N = N ⊆ proj₁ (trivialSubgroup 𝒢)
727	
728	  -- N is nontrivial: it is not contained in the trivial subgroup.
729	  Nontrivialᴺ : Pred G ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
730	  Nontrivialᴺ N = ¬ BelowTrivial N
731	```
732	
733	The two positive statements are equivalent on each side, constructively and in both
734	directions; `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction} and `Nontrivialᴺ`{.AgdaFunction} are their
735	negations, so the equivalence of the negations follows by contraposition with no
736	classical input.  We state the four positive implications first, since a downstream
737	proof usually wants one of them directly rather than the negated form.
738	
739	```agda
740	  -- If N is trivial then θ_N relates only equal elements ...
741	  below-trivial→below-diagonal : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
742	    →  BelowTrivial (set 𝑵) → BelowDiagonal 𝑮 (congruenceOf 𝑵)
743	  below-trivial→below-diagonal 𝑵 N⊆1 p = ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ (N⊆1 p)
744	
745	  -- ... and conversely, if θ_N relates only equal elements then N is trivial.
746	  below-diagonal→below-trivial : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
747	    →  BelowDiagonal 𝑮 (congruenceOf 𝑵) → BelowTrivial (set 𝑵)
748	  below-diagonal→below-trivial 𝑵 θ⊆Δ {x} x∈N = θ⊆Δ (respects (≈sym (∙ε⁻¹ x)) x∈N)
749	    where open IsSubgroup (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) using ( respects )
750	
751	  -- If θ relates only equal elements then its identity class is trivial ...
752	  con-below-diagonal→below-trivial : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ)
753	    →  BelowDiagonal 𝑮 θ → BelowTrivial (set (normalOf θ))
754	  con-below-diagonal→below-trivial θ θ⊆Δ x∈N = θ⊆Δ x∈N
755	
756	  -- ... and conversely, a trivial identity class forces θ below the diagonal.
757	  con-below-trivial→below-diagonal : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ)
758	    →  BelowTrivial (set (normalOf θ)) → BelowDiagonal 𝑮 θ
759	  con-below-trivial→below-diagonal θ N⊆1 {x} {y} p =
760	    ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ (N⊆1 (θ-trans (θ-∙ p (θ-refl {y ⁻¹})) (θ-reflexive (invʳ-law y))))
761	    where open ConNormal θ
762	```
763	
764	Negating both sides gives the statement the monolith transport needs: under the
765	correspondence, a congruence is nonzero exactly when the matching normal subgroup is
766	nontrivial.
767	
768	```agda
769	  -- θ_N is nonzero iff N is nontrivial.
770	  nonzero→nontrivial : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
771	    →  Nonzero 𝑮 (congruenceOf 𝑵) → Nontrivialᴺ (set 𝑵)
772	  nonzero→nontrivial 𝑵 nz N⊆1 = nz (below-trivial→below-diagonal 𝑵 N⊆1)
773	
774	  nontrivial→nonzero : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
775	    →  Nontrivialᴺ (set 𝑵) → Nonzero 𝑮 (congruenceOf 𝑵)
776	  nontrivial→nonzero 𝑵 nt θ⊆Δ = nt (below-diagonal→below-trivial 𝑵 θ⊆Δ)
777	
778	  -- N_θ is nontrivial iff θ is nonzero.
779	  con-nonzero→nontrivial : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ)
780	    →  Nonzero 𝑮 θ → Nontrivialᴺ (set (normalOf θ))
781	  con-nonzero→nontrivial θ nz N⊆1 = nz (con-below-trivial→below-diagonal θ N⊆1)
782	
783	  con-nontrivial→nonzero : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ)
784	    →  Nontrivialᴺ (set (normalOf θ)) → Nonzero 𝑮 θ
785	  con-nontrivial→nonzero θ nt θ⊆Δ = nt (con-below-diagonal→below-trivial θ θ⊆Δ)
786	```
787	
788	#### Simplicity across the correspondence
789	
790	The first notion to be transported whole is simplicity.  The group-theoretic
791	`IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] and the
792	congruence-level `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Simple][] are both
793	implications with a witnessed hypothesis, and under the correspondence each
794	hypothesis maps to the other: a congruence relating `a`{.AgdaBound} and
795	`b`{.AgdaBound} apart puts the non-identity element `a ∙ b ⁻¹` in the identity
796	class, and a non-identity member `x`{.AgdaBound} of a normal subgroup makes
797	`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} relate `x`{.AgdaBound} and `ε`{.AgdaFunction} apart.
798	Both directions are fully constructive, with no stability antecedent: the
799	double-negation fork recorded in the design note of
800	[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] arises only in consumers that extract identity
801	equations, and neither direction here extracts one.
802	
803	Two presentation points.  On levels: the group side at base level `ℓ₀`{.AgdaBound}
804	quantifies over subgroup predicates at `L = α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀`, so the congruence side is
805	instantiated at exactly that level, per the level-uniformity note above.  On names:
806	the two notions deliberately share the name `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction}, since they
807	live in different parameterized modules and qualified access disambiguates; here the
808	group-side notion is accessed through its defining module `Simple`{.AgdaModule} and
809	the congruence-level notion unqualified, and the theorem names spell the latter as
810	"simple algebra".
811	
812	```agda
813	  module _ (ℓ₀ : Level) where
814	    open MinimalNormal 𝒢 (ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)  using  ( IsNormalSubgroup ; isSubgroup ; isNormal )
815	
816	    -- Group-side simplicity gives congruence-level simplicity: the identity class
817	    -- of a congruence relating a distinct pair contains a non-identity element, so
818	    -- it is the whole group, so the congruence relates every pair through ε.
819	    simple→simpleAlgebra : Simple.IsSimple 𝒢 ℓ₀ → IsSimple 𝑮 (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)
820	    simple→simpleAlgebra sim θ (a , b , aθb , a≉b) x y =
821	      θ-trans (all∈N x) (θ-sym (all∈N y))
822	      where
823	      open ConNormal θ using ( θ-trans ; θ-sym )
824	
825	      𝑵 : NormalSubgroup (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)
826	      𝑵 = normalOf θ
827	
828	      -- The Σ-packaged normal subgroup, as the record the group side consumes.
829	      nsg : IsNormalSubgroup (set 𝑵)
830	      nsg = record { isSubgroup = set-isSubgroup 𝑵 ; isNormal = set-normal 𝑵 }
831	
832	      -- The round trip on congruences puts the right quotient of the related
833	      -- pair in the identity class ...
834	      ab⁻¹∈N : a ∙ b ⁻¹ ∈ set 𝑵
835	      ab⁻¹∈N = proj₂ (congruenceOf∘normalOf θ) aθb
836	
837	      -- ... and the quotient is not the identity, by cancellation.
838	      ab⁻¹≉ε : ¬ a ∙ b ⁻¹ ≈ ε
839	      ab⁻¹≉ε e = a≉b (∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ e)
840	
841	      -- Group-side simplicity applied at the witness: the class is everything.
842	      all∈N : ∀ z → z ∈ set 𝑵
843	      all∈N = sim (set 𝑵) nsg (a ∙ b ⁻¹ , ab⁻¹∈N , ab⁻¹≉ε)
844	
845	    -- Congruence-level simplicity gives group-side simplicity: the congruence of
846	    -- a normal subgroup with a non-identity member relates that member and ε
847	    -- apart, so it relates every pair, and fullness of the subgroup follows
848	    -- through the identity class.
849	    simpleAlgebra→simple : IsSimple 𝑮 (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀) → Simple.IsSimple 𝒢 ℓ₀
850	    simpleAlgebra→simple simp N nsg (x , x∈N , x≉ε) y =
851	      proj₁ (normalOf∘congruenceOf 𝑵) (simp θ (x , ε , x∼ε , x≉ε) y ε)
852	      where
853	      𝑵 : NormalSubgroup (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)
854	      𝑵 = N , isSubgroup nsg , isNormal nsg
855	
856	      θ : Con 𝑮 (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)
857	      θ = congruenceOf 𝑵
858	
859	      -- The round trip on subgroups puts the witness in the identity class of θ_N.
860	      x∼ε : proj₁ θ x ε
861	      x∼ε = proj₂ (normalOf∘congruenceOf 𝑵) x∈N
862	```

### Normal subgroups and congruences of a group

This is the [Classical.Structures.Group.Congruences][] module of the [Agda Universal Algebra Library][].

The normal subgroups of a group `𝒢` correspond to the congruences of the underlying
`Sig-Group`-algebra.  This module establishes that correspondence as an **order
isomorphism of posets**, between the congruence poset `(Con 𝑮 ℓ , ≑ , ⊑)` of
[Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][] and the poset `(NormalSubgroup ℓ , ≈ⁿ , ≤ⁿ)` of normal
subgroups under inclusion, which is built here.

Both sides carry more structure than a poset: at the absorbing level `L` the
congruences form a complete lattice ([Setoid.Congruences.CompleteLattice][]).  The
corresponding **isomorphism of complete lattices** is
[Classical.Structures.Group.NormalSubgroupLattice][], which stands on the poset
isomorphism proved here.  The split is deliberate: the correspondence below holds at
*every* relation level, whereas a lattice needs the single absorbing level at which
the join — a *generated* congruence — stays put, so bundling them would have narrowed
the theorem to the level the lattice happens to need.

The correspondence has two mutually inverse, order-preserving maps.

+  **`N ↦ θ_N`** (`congruenceOf`{.AgdaFunction}).  A normal subgroup `N` maps to the
   relation `NormalRel`{.AgdaFunction}` N`, defined by `x θ_N y ⟺ x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N`.
   We prove that this is an equivalence containing the setoid equality (for which
   `N`{.AgdaBound} being an equality-respecting subgroup is enough) and
   compatible with the three operations of `Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction}, which is where
   normality is consumed.

+  **`θ ↦ N_θ`** (`normalOf`{.AgdaFunction}).  A congruence `θ`{.AgdaBound} maps to
   the `θ`-class of the identity; we define the latter as
   `IdentityClass`{.AgdaFunction} `θ`{.AgdaBound}, which represents the predicate
   `{ x ∣ x θ ε }`.  We prove it is a normal, equality-respecting subgroup.

The two maps are monotone and mutually inverse — up to `≑`{.AgdaFunction} on
congruences and mutual inclusion on normal subgroups — so together they are an
`OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} of [Order.Iso][].

This is the bridge that `Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormal` was written
without: it lets us apply the library's `IsSubdirectlyIrreducible`{.AgdaFunction} of
[Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][] — a statement about `Con 𝑨`{.AgdaFunction} — to a
group, whose subdirect irreducibility the group theorist states as "there is a
least nontrivial normal subgroup".  The final step of that identification,
`HasMonolithᵍ → HasMonolith`, is deliberately *not* taken here; see **What this module
does and does not transport** below.

Four points about the formal statement deserve to be recorded up front, because in each
case the informal slogan "congruences are normal subgroups" conceals a choice that the
mechanized version has to make.

+  **The correspondence is level-uniform, not level-collapsing**.  It relates
   `Con 𝑮 ℓ`{.AgdaFunction} to `NormalSubgroup ℓ`{.AgdaFunction} for each *fixed*
   relation level `ℓ`{.AgdaBound}, since `NormalRel`{.AgdaFunction} of a `Pred G ℓ` is
   a `BinaryRel G ℓ` and `IdentityClass`{.AgdaFunction} of a `Con 𝑮 ℓ` is a
   `Pred G ℓ`.  It says nothing about congruences at one level versus normal subgroups
   at another.  Three instances matter downstream: `ℓ = ρ`, where the congruence side
   is the `Con 𝑮 ρ` of `IsMonolith`{.AgdaRecord} and the subgroup side contains
   `trivialSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction}, itself a `Subgroup ρ`; `ℓ = α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀`, the
   absorbing level of the congruence lattice, which is where
   [Classical.Structures.Group.NormalSubgroupLattice][] instantiates it; and
   `ℓ = α ⊔ ℓ₀`, the predicate level `L` at which `GroupSublattice 𝒢 ℓ₀`{.AgdaModule}
   of [Classical.Structures.Group.SubgroupLattice][] holds its elements, for a
   consumer that wants to compose with the *subgroup* lattice.

+  **Equality on each side is mutual containment, not propositional equality**.  On the
   congruence side this is `_≑_`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][], for
   the reasons given there (upgrading it would need propositional extensionality, which
   `--safe --cubical-compatible` does not provide); on the subgroup side we take the
   matching `_≈ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction}.  So `to∘from`{.AgdaField} and `from∘to`{.AgdaField}
   are *bi-implications of membership*, not equalities of predicates.

+  **The round trip on subgroups uses the `respects`{.AgdaField} field**.  Recovering
   `N`{.AgdaBound} from `θ_N` produces `{ x ∣ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N }`, and identifying that with
   `N`{.AgdaBound} moves membership across `x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x`.  A normal *subuniverse* that
   does not respect the setoid equality therefore need not be recovered by the round
   trip, exactly as in the respecting-interval finding of [FLRP.Bridge][].  This is why
   `NormalSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} is built on `IsSubgroup`{.AgdaRecord} (which carries
   `respects`{.AgdaField}) rather than on bare `Subuniverses`{.AgdaFunction}.

+  **Normality is consumed only by compatibility, and it is consumed exactly**.  For an
   arbitrary equality-respecting subgroup `N`{.AgdaBound}, `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction}
   is already an equivalence relation containing `_≈_`{.AgdaFunction}; this is
   `SubgroupRel`{.AgdaModule} below, and it holds with no normality hypothesis.  What
   needs normality is compatibility with `∙-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} and
   `⁻¹-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor}, so the separation is stated rather than folded
   into one monolithic lemma — and the converse `congruence→normal`{.AgdaFunction} is
   proved, so that "the correspondence is with the *normal* subgroups" is a theorem of
   the module and not a claim its prose makes on the development's behalf.

**On the choice of relation**.  `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` is the *right*-coset relation of
`N`{.AgdaBound}, whereas `Coset._∼_`{.AgdaFunction} of
[Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][] — the relation [FLRP.Bridge][] uses — is the
*left*-coset relation `x ⁻¹ ∙ y ∈ N`.  For a general subgroup the two need not agree;
for a normal subgroup they do, which we prove (`rel→coset`{.AgdaFunction},
`coset→rel`{.AgdaFunction}) rather than assume, so that either presentation may be used
downstream.

**What this module does and does not transport**.  The first notion carried whole
across the correspondence is simplicity: the final section below proves that the
group-theoretic `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] is
equivalent to the congruence-level `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of
[Setoid.Congruences.Simple][], constructively in both directions.  The retirement
program built on the correspondence also asks that `HasMonolithᵍ`{.AgdaFunction} of
`Classical.Structures.Group.MinimalNormal` be transported to
`HasMonolith`{.AgdaFunction}, that the `ᵍ` superscript be retired, and that `𝒢₂` of
`FLRP.Reductions` be restated.  Those steps remain open, with the simplicity
equivalence as their template; the `Nonzero`{.AgdaFunction}/nontriviality equivalences
proved here (`nonzero→nontrivial`{.AgdaFunction} and friends) are precisely the
ingredient the monolith transport will need beyond the isomorphism itself.

#### The ambient group

Everything below is developed inside one parameterized module, so that the group, its
carrier, its curried operations, and the conjugation vocabulary are fixed once.

```agda
module GroupCongruences {α ρ : Level} (𝒢 : Group α ρ) where
  private
    𝑮 = proj₁ 𝒢
    G = 𝕌[ 𝑮 ]

  open Setoid 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]            using  ( _≈_ )
                                renaming ( refl to ≈refl ; sym to ≈sym ; trans to ≈trans )
  open SetoidReasoning 𝔻[ 𝑮 ]
  open Group-Op 𝒢               using  ( _∙_ ; ε ; _⁻¹ ; ∙-cong ; assoc-law
                                       ; idˡ-law ; idʳ-law ; invˡ-law ; invʳ-law )
  open GroupProperties ⟨ 𝒢 ⟩ᵍᵖ  using  ( ε⁻¹≈ε ; ⁻¹-involutive ; ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙
                                       ; \\-leftDividesʳ )
  open Conjugate 𝒢                   using  ( conj-syntax ; conj-ε ; IsNormal )
```

#### Four facts of group arithmetic

The correspondence rests on four small identities, each named so that no proof below
has to inline an equational chain about them.  The first two say that `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε`
is *equivalent* to `x ≈ y` — this is what makes the relation `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` collapse to
the setoid equality exactly when `N` is trivial.  The third is right-cancellation in the
form the round trip needs, and the fourth is the unit law that identifies `x ∙ ε ⁻¹`
with `x`.

```agda
  -- x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε implies x ≈ y (multiply on the right by y).
  ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ : ∀ {x y} → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε → x ≈ y
  ∙⁻¹≈ε→≈ {x} {y} h = begin
    x               ≈˘⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
    x ∙ ε           ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (invˡ-law y) ⟩
    x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ y)  ≈˘⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) y ⟩
    x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y    ≈⟨ ∙-cong h ≈refl ⟩
    ε ∙ y           ≈⟨ idˡ-law y ⟩
    y               ∎

  -- ... and conversely, equal elements have trivial right quotient.
  ≈→∙⁻¹≈ε : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ≈ ε
  ≈→∙⁻¹≈ε {x} {y} x≈y = ≈trans (∙-cong x≈y ≈refl) (invʳ-law y)

  -- Right cancellation: the right quotient by y, multiplied back by y, is the identity.
  ∙⁻¹∙ : ∀ x y → x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y ≈ x
  ∙⁻¹∙ x y = begin
    x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∙ y    ≈⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) y ⟩
    x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ y)  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (invˡ-law y) ⟩
    x ∙ ε           ≈⟨ idʳ-law x ⟩
    x               ∎

  -- The right quotient by the identity is the identity map.
  ∙ε⁻¹ : ∀ x → x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x
  ∙ε⁻¹ x = ≈trans (∙-cong ≈refl ε⁻¹≈ε) (idʳ-law x)
```

#### Normal subgroups as an ordered object

A **normal subgroup** of `𝒢`{.AgdaBound} at predicate level `ℓ`{.AgdaBound} is a
predicate on the carrier together with a proof that it is an equality-respecting
subgroup and a proof that it is closed under conjugation.  This is
`Subgroup`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] with
`IsNormal`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Conjugation][] adjoined; it is
introduced here rather than there because normality is the *only* extra datum the
correspondence needs, and no earlier module had cause to bundle it.

Normal subgroups are ordered by inclusion of the underlying predicates, with equality
mutual inclusion — the same shape as `_⊑_`{.AgdaFunction} and `_≑_`{.AgdaFunction} on
congruences, so that the isomorphism below can be stated without any bridging
construction on either side.

```agda
  -- A normal subgroup: an equality-respecting subgroup closed under conjugation.
  NormalSubgroup : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
  NormalSubgroup ℓ = Σ[ N ∈ Pred G ℓ ] (IsSubgroup 𝒢 N × IsNormal N)

  -- The underlying predicate of a normal subgroup ...
  set : NormalSubgroup ℓ → Pred G ℓ
  set (N , _ , _) = N

  -- ... and its two proof components.
  set-isSubgroup : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → IsSubgroup 𝒢 (set 𝑵)
  set-isSubgroup (_ , isSubgroup , _) = isSubgroup

  set-normal : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → IsNormal (set 𝑵)
  set-normal (_ , _ , isNormal) = isNormal

  infix 4 _≤ⁿ_ _≈ⁿ_

  -- The inclusion order on normal subgroups ...
  _≤ⁿ_ : NormalSubgroup ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 = set 𝑴 ⊆ set 𝑵

  -- ... and the equivalence of mutual inclusion it is antisymmetric over.
  _≈ⁿ_ : NormalSubgroup ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ℓ)
  𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 = 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 × 𝑵 ≤ⁿ 𝑴
```

Calling the correspondence an *order* isomorphism presupposes that both sides really
are ordered, so the partial-order laws are proved rather than assumed.  They are the
laws of `_⊆_`{.AgdaFunction} on predicates, and antisymmetry holds by construction:
`_≈ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction} *is* mutual inclusion.  This mirrors
`⊆-isPartialOrder`{.AgdaFunction} and `Con-Poset`{.AgdaFunction} on the congruence
side, down to the same implicit-argument discipline — `_≤ⁿ_`{.AgdaFunction} is a
defined relation, not an injective type former, so Agda cannot recover the endpoint
arguments of the helper lemmas from the expected field types and they are forwarded by
hand.

```agda
  ≤ⁿ-refl : {𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑵 ≤ⁿ 𝑵
  ≤ⁿ-refl p = p

  ≤ⁿ-trans : {𝑳 𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑳 ≤ⁿ 𝑴 → 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑳 ≤ⁿ 𝑵
  ≤ⁿ-trans 𝑳≤𝑴 𝑴≤𝑵 p = 𝑴≤𝑵 (𝑳≤𝑴 p)

  ≈ⁿ-refl : {𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑵 ≈ⁿ 𝑵
  ≈ⁿ-refl = (λ p → p) , (λ p → p)

  ≈ⁿ-sym : {𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑵 ≈ⁿ 𝑴
  ≈ⁿ-sym = swap

  ≈ⁿ-trans : {𝑳 𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ} → 𝑳 ≈ⁿ 𝑴 → 𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → 𝑳 ≈ⁿ 𝑵
  ≈ⁿ-trans (𝑳≤𝑴 , 𝑴≤𝑳) (𝑴≤𝑵 , 𝑵≤𝑴) = (λ p → 𝑴≤𝑵 (𝑳≤𝑴 p)) , (λ p → 𝑴≤𝑳 (𝑵≤𝑴 p))

  ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ})
  ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence {ℓ} = record
    { refl   = λ {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-refl {ℓ} {𝑵}
    ; sym    = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-sym {ℓ} {𝑴} {𝑵}
    ; trans  = λ {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≈ⁿ-trans {ℓ} {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵}
    }

  ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder : IsPartialOrder (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ}) _≤ⁿ_
  ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder {ℓ} = record
    { isPreorder = record  { isEquivalence  = ≈ⁿ-isEquivalence {ℓ}
                           ; reflexive      = proj₁
                           ; trans          = λ {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵} → ≤ⁿ-trans {ℓ} {𝑳} {𝑴} {𝑵}
                           }
    ; antisym = _,_
    }

  -- The poset of normal subgroups, the counterpart of `Con-Poset` of
  -- [Setoid.Congruences.Lattice][].
  NormalSubgroup-Poset : (ℓ : Level) → Poset (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ) (α ⊔ ℓ)
  NormalSubgroup-Poset ℓ = record  { Carrier         = NormalSubgroup ℓ
                                   ; _≈_             = _≈ⁿ_
                                   ; _≤_             = _≤ⁿ_
                                   ; isPartialOrder  = ≤ⁿ-isPartialOrder
                                   }
```

#### The relation attached to a subgroup

`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is the relation "`x` and `y` differ by an element of
`N`", written with the *right* quotient `x ∙ y ⁻¹`.  It is defined for an arbitrary
predicate, so that the hypotheses each of its properties needs can be stated exactly.

```agda
  -- x and y are related when their right quotient lies in N.
  NormalRel : Pred G ℓ → BinaryRel G ℓ
  NormalRel N x y = x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N
```

For an equality-respecting subgroup `N`{.AgdaBound} — with no normality hypothesis —
`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is an equivalence relation that contains the setoid
equality.  Each clause is one closure property of `N`{.AgdaBound} transported along one
line of group arithmetic, exactly as in `Coset`{.AgdaModule} of
[Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][] for the left-handed relation.

```agda
  module SubgroupRel {ℓ : Level} (N : Pred G ℓ) (N-sg : IsSubgroup 𝒢 N) where

    open IsSubgroup N-sg  using ( respects ; ∙-closed ; ε-closed ; ⁻¹-closed )

    infix 4 _∼_

    _∼_ : BinaryRel G ℓ
    _∼_ = NormalRel N

    -- Reflexivity is ε ∈ N transported along x ∙ x ⁻¹ ≈ ε.
    ∼-refl : ∀ {x} → x ∼ x
    ∼-refl {x} = respects (≈sym (invʳ-law x)) ε-closed

    -- Symmetry is closure under inverses, since (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ∙ x ⁻¹.
    ∼-sym : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → y ∼ x
    ∼-sym {x} {y} x∼y = respects inv-eq (⁻¹-closed x∼y)
      where
      inv-eq : (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ∙ x ⁻¹
      inv-eq = begin
        (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⁻¹     ≈⟨ ⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ x (y ⁻¹) ⟩
        (y ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ∙ x ⁻¹  ≈⟨ ∙-cong (⁻¹-involutive y) ≈refl ⟩
        y ∙ x ⁻¹          ∎

    -- Transitivity is closure under products, since (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ z ⁻¹.
    ∼-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x ∼ y → y ∼ z → x ∼ z
    ∼-trans {x} {y} {z} x∼y y∼z = respects prod-eq (∙-closed x∼y y∼z)
      where
      prod-eq : (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ z ⁻¹
      prod-eq = begin
        (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹)  ≈⟨ assoc-law x (y ⁻¹) (y ∙ z ⁻¹) ⟩
        x ∙ (y ⁻¹ ∙ (y ∙ z ⁻¹))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ y (z ⁻¹)) ⟩
        x ∙ z ⁻¹                 ∎

    ∼-isEquivalence : IsEquivalence _∼_
    ∼-isEquivalence = record { refl = ∼-refl ; sym = ∼-sym ; trans = ∼-trans }

    -- The setoid equality refines the relation (this is the `reflexive` field a
    -- congruence must supply, and it is what makes the relation contain the diagonal).
    ≈⇒∼ : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x ∼ y
    ≈⇒∼ x≈y = respects (≈sym (≈→∙⁻¹≈ε x≈y)) ε-closed

    -- Consequently the relation may be transported along ≈ in either argument.
    ∼-resp : ∀ {x x' y y'} → x ≈ x' → y ≈ y' → x ∼ y → x' ∼ y'
    ∼-resp x≈x' y≈y' p = ∼-trans (∼-trans (≈⇒∼ (≈sym x≈x')) p) (≈⇒∼ y≈y')
```

#### From a normal subgroup to a congruence

Adding normality makes the relation compatible with the three operations of
`Sig-Group`{.AgdaFunction}, hence a congruence.

Compatibility with `∙-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} is the substantive clause and the
only one that uses normality in an essential way: from `x ∙ y ⁻¹ ∈ N` and
`u ∙ v ⁻¹ ∈ N` we must produce `(x ∙ u) ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹ ∈ N`, and the two given elements do
not multiply to it — one of them must first be *moved past* `x`{.AgdaBound}, which is
precisely conjugation.  Compatibility with `⁻¹-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} is one
conjugation as well; with `ε-Op`{.AgdaInductiveConstructor} it is reflexivity.

```agda
  module NormalCon {ℓ : Level} (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) where

    private
      N : Pred G ℓ
      N = set 𝑵

    open IsSubgroup (set-isSubgroup 𝑵)  using ( respects ; ∙-closed )
    open SubgroupRel N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) public

    normal : IsNormal N
    normal = set-normal 𝑵

    -- Compatibility with the curried multiplication.  The element x ∙ y ⁻¹ is on the
    -- wrong side of x ∙ u, so u ∙ v ⁻¹ is first conjugated by x — the one step that
    -- normality supplies and that fails for a non-normal subgroup.
    ∼-∙ : ∀ {x y u v} → x ∼ y → u ∼ v → (x ∙ u) ∼ (y ∙ v)
    ∼-∙ {x} {y} {u} {v} p q = respects step (∙-closed (normal x q) p)
      where
      step : x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ≈ x ∙ u ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹
      step = begin
        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹)    ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹)) (x ⁻¹) (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ⟩
        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ (x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹))  ≈⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (\\-leftDividesʳ x (y ⁻¹)) ⟩
        x ∙ (u ∙ v ⁻¹) ∙ y ⁻¹                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong (assoc-law x u (v ⁻¹)) ≈refl ⟩
        x ∙ u ∙ v ⁻¹ ∙ y ⁻¹                   ≈⟨ assoc-law (x ∙ u) (v ⁻¹) (y ⁻¹) ⟩
        x ∙ u ∙ (v ⁻¹ ∙ y ⁻¹)                 ≈˘⟨ ∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-anti-homo-∙ y v) ⟩
        x ∙ u ∙ (y ∙ v) ⁻¹                    ∎

    -- Compatibility with the curried inverse: conjugating x ∙ y ⁻¹ by x ⁻¹ produces
    -- y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹, which is the relation the other way round.
    ∼-⁻¹ : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → x ⁻¹ ∼ y ⁻¹
    ∼-⁻¹ {x} {y} p = ∼-sym (respects step (normal (x ⁻¹) p))
      where
      step : x ⁻¹ ∙ (x ∙ y ⁻¹) ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹ ≈ y ⁻¹ ∙ (x ⁻¹) ⁻¹
      step = ∙-cong (\\-leftDividesʳ x (y ⁻¹)) ≈refl

    -- Compatibility with every operation symbol.  Each clause is the corresponding
    -- curried fact, transported across the tuple-vs-curried interpretation bridges of
    -- [Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups].
    ∼-compatible : 𝑮 ∣≈ _∼_
    ∼-compatible ∙-Op   {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 u))
                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-∙ 𝒢 v))
                                            (∼-∙ (p 0F) (p 1F))
    ∼-compatible ε-Op   {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 u))
                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-ε 𝒢 v))
                                            ∼-refl
    ∼-compatible ⁻¹-Op  {u} {v} p = ∼-resp  (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 u))
                                            (≈sym (interp-tuple-⁻¹ 𝒢 v))
                                            (∼-⁻¹ (p 0F))

    -- The relation of a normal subgroup is a congruence of the group algebra.
    ∼-isCongruence : IsCongruence 𝑮 _∼_
    ∼-isCongruence = mkcon ≈⇒∼ ∼-isEquivalence ∼-compatible
```

For a normal subgroup the right-handed relation used here agrees with the left-handed
coset relation `Coset._∼_`{.AgdaFunction} of [Classical.Structures.Group.Cosets][],
which is the one [FLRP.Bridge][] builds on.  Both directions are one application of
`∼-⁻¹`{.AgdaFunction} followed by an involutivity rewrite, so nothing about the
development depends on which of the two presentations a consumer prefers.

```agda
    -- The right-coset relation of a normal subgroup is its left-coset relation ...
    rel→coset : ∀ {x y} → x ∼ y → Coset._∼_ 𝒢 N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) x y
    rel→coset {x} {y} p = respects (∙-cong ≈refl (⁻¹-involutive y)) (∼-⁻¹ p)

    -- ... and conversely.
    coset→rel : ∀ {x y} → Coset._∼_ 𝒢 N (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) x y → x ∼ y
    coset→rel {x} {y} p = ∼-resp  (⁻¹-involutive x) (⁻¹-involutive y)
                                  (∼-⁻¹ (respects (∙-cong ≈refl (≈sym (⁻¹-involutive y))) p))
```

The forward map of the correspondence packages the relation with its congruence proof.

```agda
  -- N ↦ θ_N : a normal subgroup gives a congruence of the group algebra.
  congruenceOf : NormalSubgroup ℓ → Con 𝑮 ℓ
  congruenceOf 𝑵 = NormalRel (set 𝑵) , NormalCon.∼-isCongruence 𝑵
```

#### From a congruence to a normal subgroup

In the other direction the ingredients are the curried consequences of a congruence's
compatibility: it is preserved by multiplication, by inversion, and hence by
conjugation.  These are read off from `is-compatible`{.AgdaFunction} at the canonical
tuples, with no interpretation bridge needed — the curried accessors of
`Group-Op`{.AgdaModule} are *defined* by applying the interpreted symbol to exactly
those tuples.

```agda
  module ConNormal {ℓ : Level} ((_θ_ , θcon) : Con 𝑮 ℓ) where

    -- The equivalence laws of θ, read off the record.
    θ-refl : ∀ {x} → x θ x
    θ-refl = IsEquivalence.refl (is-equivalence θcon)

    θ-sym : ∀ {x y} → x θ y → y θ x
    θ-sym = IsEquivalence.sym (is-equivalence θcon)

    θ-trans : ∀ {x y z} → x θ y → y θ z → x θ z
    θ-trans = IsEquivalence.trans (is-equivalence θcon)

    -- A congruence relates ≈-equal elements.
    θ-reflexive : ∀ {x y} → x ≈ y → x θ y
    θ-reflexive = reflexive θcon

    -- Compatibility with the curried multiplication ...
    θ-∙ : ∀ {x y u v} → x θ y → u θ v → (x ∙ u) θ (y ∙ v)
    θ-∙ {x} {y} {u} {v} p q = is-compatible θcon ∙-Op λ { 0F → p ; 1F → q }

    -- ... and with the curried inverse.
    θ-⁻¹ : ∀ {x y} → x θ y → (x ⁻¹) θ (y ⁻¹)
    θ-⁻¹ p = is-compatible θcon ⁻¹-Op (λ _ → p)

    -- Hence conjugation by any element preserves the congruence.
    θ-conj : ∀ g {x y} → x θ y → x ^ g θ y ^ g
    θ-conj g {x} {y} p = θ-∙ (θ-∙ (θ-refl {x = g}) p) (θ-refl {x = g ⁻¹})
```

The class of the identity is an equality-respecting subgroup, and it is normal.
Membership is `x θ ε`, so each subgroup law is one application of the corresponding
compatibility fact followed by a `≈`-step that renormalizes the right-hand side back to
`ε`{.AgdaFunction}: `ε ∙ ε ≈ ε`, `ε ⁻¹ ≈ ε`, and `conj g ε ≈ ε`.

```agda
    -- The θ-class of the identity.
    IdentityClass : Pred G ℓ
    IdentityClass x = x θ ε

    -- It respects the setoid equality, because a congruence contains it.
    IdentityClass-respects : IdentityClass Respects _≈_
    IdentityClass-respects x≈y p = θ-trans (θ-reflexive (≈sym x≈y)) p

    IdentityClass-ε : ε ∈ IdentityClass
    IdentityClass-ε = θ-refl

    IdentityClass-∙ : ∀ {x y} → x ∈ IdentityClass → y ∈ IdentityClass
      → x ∙ y ∈ IdentityClass
    IdentityClass-∙ p q = θ-trans (θ-∙ p q) (θ-reflexive (idˡ-law ε))

    IdentityClass-⁻¹ : ∀ {x} → x ∈ IdentityClass → x ⁻¹ ∈ IdentityClass
    IdentityClass-⁻¹ p = θ-trans (θ-⁻¹ p) (θ-reflexive ε⁻¹≈ε)

    -- The identity class is an equality-respecting subgroup ...
    IdentityClass-isSubgroup : IsSubgroup 𝒢 IdentityClass
    IdentityClass-isSubgroup = mkIsSubgroup 𝒢  IdentityClass-respects IdentityClass-∙
                                               IdentityClass-ε IdentityClass-⁻¹

    -- ... and it is normal, since conjugation fixes the identity.
    IdentityClass-normal : IsNormal IdentityClass
    IdentityClass-normal g p = θ-trans (θ-conj g p) (θ-reflexive (conj-ε g))
```

The backward map of the correspondence packages the class with its two proofs.

```agda
  -- θ ↦ N_θ : a congruence gives a normal subgroup of the group.
  normalOf : Con 𝑮 ℓ → NormalSubgroup ℓ
  normalOf θ =  ConNormal.IdentityClass θ
             ,  ConNormal.IdentityClass-isSubgroup θ
             ,  ConNormal.IdentityClass-normal θ
```

#### Normality is necessary, not merely sufficient

`NormalCon`{.AgdaModule} shows normality *suffices* for `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} to
be a congruence.  The converse holds too, and is worth proving rather than asserting:
were it left as prose, the claim "the correspondence is with the *normal* subgroups"
would be doing work the formal development had not done, and nothing would rule out the
relation of some non-normal subgroup slipping into `Con 𝑮 ℓ`{.AgdaFunction}.

The proof needs no new group arithmetic.  If `NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} is a
congruence, its identity class is normal by
`IdentityClass-normal`{.AgdaFunction} — and that class is
`{ x ∣ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N }`, which `respects`{.AgdaField} identifies with
`N`{.AgdaBound} itself.

```agda
  -- If the relation of an equality-respecting subgroup is a congruence, the subgroup
  -- is normal.  With `NormalCon.∼-isCongruence` this makes normality *equivalent* to
  -- compatibility, so `NormalSubgroup ℓ` is exactly the source of the correspondence.
  congruence→normal : {ℓ : Level} (N : Pred G ℓ) → IsSubgroup 𝒢 N
    →  IsCongruence 𝑮 (NormalRel N) → IsNormal N
  congruence→normal N N-sg isCon g {x} x∈N =
    respects  (∙ε⁻¹ (x ^ g))
              (ConNormal.IdentityClass-normal (NormalRel N , isCon) g
                (respects (≈sym (∙ε⁻¹ x)) x∈N))
    where open IsSubgroup N-sg using ( respects )
```

#### Monotonicity

Both maps act by (co)restriction of the underlying predicates and relations, so
monotonicity is immediate in each direction.

```agda
  -- The congruence-to-subgroup map is monotone.
  normalOf-mono : (θ φ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → θ ⊑ φ → normalOf θ ≤ⁿ normalOf φ
  normalOf-mono _ _ θ⊑φ p = θ⊑φ p

  -- The subgroup-to-congruence map is monotone.
  congruenceOf-mono : (𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → 𝑴 ≤ⁿ 𝑵 → congruenceOf 𝑴 ⊑ congruenceOf 𝑵
  congruenceOf-mono _ _ 𝑴≤𝑵 p = 𝑴≤𝑵 p
```

`OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} asks only for monotonicity, not for the maps to be well defined
on equivalence classes, so that latter property — which "isomorphism of posets" is
usually taken to include — is recorded here rather than left implicit.  It costs
nothing: each equivalence *is* mutual containment, so applying the matching
monotonicity twice suffices.

```agda
  -- Both maps respect the equivalences of the two sides.
  normalOf-cong : (θ φ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → θ ≑ φ → normalOf θ ≈ⁿ normalOf φ
  normalOf-cong  θ φ (θ⊑φ , φ⊑θ) =
    normalOf-mono θ φ θ⊑φ , normalOf-mono φ θ φ⊑θ

  congruenceOf-cong : (𝑴 𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
    →  𝑴 ≈ⁿ 𝑵 → congruenceOf 𝑴 ≑ congruenceOf 𝑵
  congruenceOf-cong 𝑴 𝑵 (𝑴≤𝑵 , 𝑵≤𝑴) =
    congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵 𝑴≤𝑵 , congruenceOf-mono 𝑵 𝑴 𝑵≤𝑴
```

#### Mutual inverseness

On congruences, `θ_{N_θ} ≑ θ`: the relation `θ_{N_θ}` holds at `(x , y)` when
`(x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε`, and multiplying on the right by `y`{.AgdaBound} converts that to
`x θ y` through `∙⁻¹∙`{.AgdaFunction} and the unit law — while multiplying `x θ y` on
the right by `y ⁻¹` converts it back through `invʳ-law`{.AgdaFunction}.

```agda
  -- Round trip on congruences: θ_{N_θ} ≑ θ.
  congruenceOf∘normalOf : (θ : Con 𝑮 ℓ) → congruenceOf (normalOf θ) ≑ θ
  congruenceOf∘normalOf θ = fwd , bwd
    where
    open ConNormal θ

    -- From (x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε derive x θ y.
    fwd : congruenceOf (normalOf θ) ⊑ θ
    fwd {x} {y} p = θ-trans  (θ-reflexive (≈sym (∙⁻¹∙ x y)))
                             (θ-trans (θ-∙ p θ-refl) (θ-reflexive (idˡ-law y)))

    -- From x θ y derive (x ∙ y ⁻¹) θ ε.
    bwd : θ ⊑ congruenceOf (normalOf θ)
    bwd {x} {y} p = θ-trans (θ-∙ p (θ-refl {y ⁻¹})) (θ-reflexive (invʳ-law y))
```

On normal subgroups, `N_{θ_N} ≈ⁿ N`: an element `x`{.AgdaBound} lies in `N_{θ_N}` when
`x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N`, and `x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x`, so the `respects`{.AgdaField} proof carried by the
subgroup identifies the two.  **This is the step that consumes the
`respects`{.AgdaField} field**, and the sole place the correspondence would break for a
normal subuniverse not closed under the setoid equality.

```agda
  -- Round trip on normal subgroups: N_{θ_N} ≈ⁿ N (needs the respecting field).
  normalOf∘congruenceOf : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ) → normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵) ≈ⁿ 𝑵
  normalOf∘congruenceOf 𝑵 = fwd , bwd
    where
    open IsSubgroup (set-isSubgroup 𝑵) using ( respects )

    -- x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N and x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ≈ x give x ∈ N.
    fwd : normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵) ≤ⁿ 𝑵
    fwd {x} p = respects (∙ε⁻¹ x) p

    -- x ∈ N and x ≈ x ∙ ε ⁻¹ give x ∙ ε ⁻¹ ∈ N.
    bwd : 𝑵 ≤ⁿ normalOf (congruenceOf 𝑵)
    bwd {x} p = respects (≈sym (∙ε⁻¹ x)) p
```

#### The order isomorphism

Assembling the four facts — two maps, both monotone, mutually inverse — gives the
correspondence as an `OrderIso`{.AgdaRecord} between the congruence containment order of
the group algebra and the inclusion order on normal subgroups.  (The endpoint implicits
of the monotone maps are bound and forwarded explicitly: `Con`{.AgdaFunction} and
`NormalSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} are defined functions, not injective type formers, so
Agda cannot recover them from the field types.)

```agda
  -- The order isomorphism Con 𝑮 ℓ ≅ NormalSubgroup ℓ.
  NormalCongruenceIso : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
  NormalCongruenceIso ℓ =
    OrderIso (_≑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ}) (_⊑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ}) (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ}) (_≤ⁿ_ {ℓ})

  normal-congruence-iso : (ℓ : Level) → NormalCongruenceIso ℓ
  normal-congruence-iso ℓ = record
    { to         = normalOf
    ; from       = congruenceOf
    ; to-mono    = λ {θ} {φ} → normalOf-mono θ φ
    ; from-mono  = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵
    ; to∘from    = normalOf∘congruenceOf
    ; from∘to    = congruenceOf∘normalOf
    }
```

The reverse isomorphism presents the normal subgroups of `𝒢`{.AgdaBound} as the
congruence poset of its underlying algebra — the form a representability argument wants.

```agda
  NormalCongruenceIso⁻¹ : (ℓ : Level) → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ suc ℓ)
  NormalCongruenceIso⁻¹ ℓ =
    OrderIso (_≈ⁿ_ {ℓ}) (_≤ⁿ_ {ℓ}) (_≑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ}) (_⊑_ {𝑨 = 𝑮} {ℓ = ℓ})

  normal-congruence-iso⁻¹ : (ℓ : Level) → NormalCongruenceIso⁻¹ ℓ
  normal-congruence-iso⁻¹ ℓ = record
    { to         = congruenceOf
    ; from       = normalOf
    ; to-mono    = λ {𝑴} {𝑵} → congruenceOf-mono 𝑴 𝑵
    ; from-mono  = λ {θ} {φ} → normalOf-mono θ φ
    ; to∘from    = congruenceOf∘normalOf
    ; from∘to    = normalOf∘congruenceOf
    }
```

#### Nonzero congruences and nontrivial normal subgroups

The order isomorphism alone does not say that the two sides agree on which elements are
*above the bottom*; that has to be proved, and it is what the monolith transport will
consume.  The bottom of the subgroup side is `trivialSubgroup`{.AgdaFunction} of
[Classical.Structures.Group.Subgroups][] — the `≈`-class of the identity, which over a
setoid carrier is the right notion of the one-element subgroup — and the bottom of the
congruence side is the diagonal, whose "at the bottom" predicate is
`BelowDiagonal`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Monolith][].

```agda
  -- N is contained in the trivial subgroup { x ∣ x ≈ ε }.
  BelowTrivial : Pred G ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  BelowTrivial N = N ⊆ proj₁ (trivialSubgroup 𝒢)

  -- N is nontrivial: it is not contained in the trivial subgroup.
  Nontrivialᴺ : Pred G ℓ → Type (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ)
  Nontrivialᴺ N = ¬ BelowTrivial N
```

The two positive statements are equivalent on each side, constructively and in both

negations, so the equivalence of the negations follows by contraposition with no
classical input.  We state the four positive implications first, since a downstream
proof usually wants one of them directly rather than the negated form.

```agda

  below-diagonal→below-trivial : (𝑵 : NormalSubgroup ℓ)
```


The first notion to be transported whole is simplicity.  The group-theoretic

congruence-level `IsSimple`{.AgdaFunction} of [Setoid.Congruences.Simple][] are both
implications with a witnessed hypothesis, and under the correspondence each
hypothesis maps to the other: a congruence relating `a`{.AgdaBound} and
`b`{.AgdaBound} apart puts the non-identity element `a ∙ b ⁻¹` in the identity

`NormalRel N`{.AgdaFunction} relate `x`{.AgdaBound} and `ε`{.AgdaFunction} apart.

double-negation fork recorded in the design note of
[Classical.Structures.Group.Simple][] arises only in consumers that extract identity
equations, and neither direction here extracts one.

```agda
    -- of a congruence relating a distinct pair contains a non-identity element, so
    -- it is the whole group, so the congruence relates every pair through ε.
    simple→simpleAlgebra : Simple.IsSimple 𝒢 ℓ₀ → IsSimple 𝑮 (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)

      θ-trans (all∈N x) (θ-sym (all∈N y))

      open ConNormal θ using ( θ-trans ; θ-sym )

      𝑵 : NormalSubgroup (α ⊔ ρ ⊔ ℓ₀)

      -- The Σ-packaged normal subgroup, as the record the group side consumes.

      -- The round trip on congruences puts the right quotient of the related
      -- pair in the identity class ...

    -- a normal subgroup with a non-identity member relates that member and ε
    -- apart, so it relates every pair, and fullness of the subgroup follows
    -- through the identity class.

      θ = congruenceOf 𝑵

      x∼ε : proj₁ θ x ε
```
